title.en: Three.js scene assembly and transform adapter

summary: Map semantic parts to stable scene nodes with deliberate local and world coordinate ownership.
objective: Moving the assembly root moves all intended parts exactly once; moving a joint leaves its support in place.
example_prompts: Map semantic parts to stable scene nodes with deliberate local and world coordinate ownership.

principles: Use semantic assembly IDs independently of mesh names and rendering detail.
Keep decorative transforms beneath the node that owns the functional pose.
implementation: Create one root per selectable assembly and child groups for moving subassemblies. Keep an explicit ID-to-node map.
Object3D matrix is local and matrixWorld is world space; declare which space each input and model output uses.
For inspection, preserve the simulation hierarchy and use presentation offsets or a separate view copy. Dispose owned geometry and materials when replacing an assembly.
observable_checks: Moving the assembly root moves all intended parts exactly once; moving a joint leaves its support in place.
Return from inspection restores the original transform values and selection identity.

known_limits: Three.js transform hierarchy does not enforce mechanical joints or contact. Resource cleanup depends on ownership and installed APIs.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: Object3D exposes child nodes and distinct local and world transformation matrices.
